data.cultural_impact: The name Utsman in the Islamic context has a significant historical meaning, particularly for the early Islamic community. Utsman ibn Affan (652 AD – 656 AD) was the third Caliph, succeeding Abu Bakr and Umar ibn Al-Khattab. Utsman played a pivotal role in the early Islamic hegira (migration) to Medina from Mecca and played a major role in the consolidation of the Islamic state during the reigns of the first two Caliphs. His name remains a reminder of this critical period in Islamic history and serves as a representation of the importance of unity, leadership, and stability.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Utsman or Uthman is a reflection of the character and values that are cherished in the Islamic tradition. The name can be interpreted as meaning "he who settles, resides, or dwells." In a spiritual context, this can be seen as the essence of a believer's journey towards self-realization and a closer relationship with Allah (God). The name calls upon an individual to find a deep sense of peace and tranquility within oneself and to live a life in accordance with the guidance and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Through this, the name serves as a reminder that no matter where we may physically reside, the true home of every believer is within their own heart, connected to Allah, and that striving to live a life of righteousness and devotion to Allah brings peace and spiritual fulfillment.

historical_references.reference: Uthman ibn Affan was the third caliph (successor) of Muhammad, the prophet of Islam. He ruled from 656 to 658 CE. Uthman is considered to be the first orthodox caliph as he upheld the Quran as the fundamental law of the Islamic state. His caliphate was a period of relative stability and continuity, following the turbulence and instability of the Rashidun Caliphs. He was assassinated in his residence in Medina in 656 CE.
historical_references.context: He was the third caliph and the first orthodox caliph of Islam

historical_references.reference: Uthman ibn Affan is notable for the compilation of the standard version of the Quran, known as the Uthmanic codex, during his caliphate. The Quran was initially written on parchment, bones and palm leaves, and Uthman ordered a standardized version to be produced in order to prevent any confusion or misinterpretations. The Uthmanic codex is the version of the Quran that is currently used by Muslims worldwide.
historical_references.context: He ordered the compilation of the standardized version of the Quran
